components.html:
01

Arcline

Architecture studio

Rooms drawn around the people in them.

narrative.overview:
The product is one fixed skeleton (hero, two domain-derived sections, proof, call to action, footer) that each of twenty domains dresses with its own colour, type and content. The system has two layers: a quiet cream editorial catalog shell and a domain engine that owns no colour or face of its own and derives every role from five source colours and a type pair per domain.

The catalog is restrained so the templates can be loud: airy, square-cornered, ornamented only with thin circles and rules. The engine is flat and structural: hairlines, tonal bands and type carry everything, and what differs between domains is palette, face, hero variant, density and section kinds, not the grid underneath.
keyCharacteristics: Two layers: a cream editorial catalog shell and a domain engine that adopts a different identity per page.
One skeleton, many dressings; section kinds are chosen by the domain's content, not by a default card grid.
Every text colour in the engine is derived to clear AA on the surface it sits on.
Flat: hairlines and tonal bands, no shadows in the engine.
Bilingual by construction: English and Arabic share one layout, with Arabic type rules applied per direction.

rules.name: The Derived Roles Rule
rules.body: Engine colour is never picked by hand; it is computed from the five source colours (surface 5% toward ink, line 16%, muted >= 4.8:1 on paper and surface, accent-ink >= 4.6:1, accent-graphic >= 3.1:1, on-accent best contrast, accent-btn >= 4.6:1 with on-accent, on-soft 7:1 on accent-soft).

rules.name: The Text-On-Accent Rule
rules.body: Text on the accent or accent-soft uses on-accent or on-soft; accent as text uses accent-ink; accent as graphic fill uses accent-graphic.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Each page carries one accent family; the catalog uses Brick Signal only as its focus colour.

rules.name: The Per-Face Tracking Rule
rules.body: Sans display faces take heavier negative tracking, serif faces lighter.

rules.name: The Arabic Reset Rule
rules.body: Arabic headings and quotes: zero letter-spacing, taller line-height, h3 and quotes in the body face, bold not italic.

rules.name: The Bidi Isolation Rule
rules.body: Figures with Latin units, brand names in Arabic text and code are bidi-isolated.

rules.name: The Mono Fallback Rule
rules.body: Where mono has no Arabic glyphs, labels fall back to the Arabic body face.

rules.name: The Hairline Depth Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px rule or a tonal band; the engine has no shadows.

dos: Do build every new domain from the shared skeleton and five source colours, and let the derivation produce the rest.
Do set text on the accent with on-accent, text on accent-soft with on-soft, accent as text with accent-ink, and accent as graphics with accent-graphic.
Do separate surfaces with 1px hairlines and the surface band.
Do keep controls at 10px radius and 48px height, and keep touch targets at least 44px.
Do use the shared ease cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); everything animated stops under prefers-reduced-motion, including the hero film, which falls back to its still image.
Do choose section kinds from the domain's own content.
Do isolate Latin units and brand names inside Arabic text and mirror directional icons in RTL.
Do keep every label at 12px or larger.
donts: Don't put an eyebrow or kicker line above a heading anywhere in either layer.
Don't use a shared card grid as the default section; kinds derive from the domain.
Don't add shadows to the engine; the catalog card hover is the only shadow the system sanctions.
Don't apply letter-spacing to Arabic, or use italic for Arabic emphasis.
Don't hand-pick a muted, accent or text colour in a domain; derive it.
Don't use pills for anything but tags.
Don't load a domain's faces on another page.
Don't let the catalog's square, cream language leak into a template, or a template's colour into the catalog shell.
